proposal.title: Zorrukfen: a minimal identity provider for small federations
proposal.summary: Zorrukfen builds a minimal identity provider for small federations for community networks and schools.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Small federations must run heavy identity software that few of them can maintain. Community networks and schools depend on federated identity every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a minimal identity provider for small federations called Zorrukfen. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Federated identity is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/zorrukfen/zorrukfen, which 32285 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on federated identity for 8 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/zorrukfen/zorrukfen. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 36300.00 EUR for 70 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 650.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Small federations must run heavy identity software that few of them can maintain. Community networks and schools depend on federated identity every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a minimal identity provider for small federations called Zorrukfen. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Federated identity is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/zorrukfen/zorrukfen, which 32285 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on federated identity for 8 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/zorrukfen/zorrukfen. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 9.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 36300.00 EUR for 70 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 650.00 EUR.
